title: mobile.de, Auto Trader and AutoScout24: Lessons from Automotive Marketplaces
basis: Reconstructed on 2026-11-12 from the published index.md (paragraph for paragraph, in its own order) and spec.md (accepted 2026-10-21), which it replaces. Intent outcome, the five journal acceptance criteria, the thesis and the role are copied unchanged from the case-automotive entry in journal-spec.json. Added: a roadmap paragraph (p04), a one-sentence lead-in to the vertical-differences table (p49), and a conclusion section that performs Part IX's closing (p64 to p66; the published closing paragraph is split across p64, p65 and p66, its sentences kept).

know: Why automotive behaves differently: a car carries a machine-readable identity, most cars are listed by dealers through software, and the dealer who supplies the stock is also the paying customer.

mobile.de's architecture as written in its APIs (transfer service providers as integration principals, idempotent creates, one write at a time per ad, taxonomy keyed to a vehicle derivative, the price rating as a resource, a change feed with a 24-hour catch-up window); Autotrader UK's disclosed levers, data APIs and Deal Builder; AutoScout24's platform story; CarGurus' price transparency and the CarOffer wind-down; OLX Autos as the contrast.

Price evaluation as a control loop across the cases (five-band ratings, no-rating paths, dealer tools that show how a price change moves the band or the search position) and where the evidence stops (mobile.de internals, AutoScout24's product platform, all valuation methods).
believe: In automotive the published dealer contract is the architecture document.

A price rating that feeds ranking or dealer tools needs the governance of a ranking model, and platform-controlled states on a dealer's stock are commercial-model changes that must be opt-in and reversible.
can_do: Write the commitments of a professional supply contract (accountable integrators, idempotent creates, one writer per listing, stable error keys, a change feed with replay, a notice period).
Decide how far up the transaction ladder a marketplace should go and what evidence would justify each step.

audience.who: Chief and enterprise architects, principal engineers and engineering leaders of vertical or multi-vertical marketplace groups, especially those running dealer-fed automotive brands or deciding how far a marketplace should reach into the transaction.
already_knows: What an API, a database, an event stream, a search engine and Kubernetes are, and ML serving.
Part IX's evidence rules, from part-9, and the five earlier cases.

Feed contracts (listing-ingestion), change feeds (event-driven-listings), enrichment (normalization-and-enrichment), model governance by decision (ml-platform), ranking (ranking), entitlements (products-and-entitlements) and the automotive requirement profile (vertical-requirements).
Veldmark and its automotive brand Motorvane, from meet-veldmark and the chapters.
does_not_know: The automotive companies' corporate histories and products (mobile.de, Autotrader UK, AutoScout24, CarGurus, OLX Autos).
Automotive integration terms: transfer service provider (TSP), dealer management system (DMS), Germany's type-approval codes (HSN/TSN).
The metrics ARPR (average revenue per retailer) and IMV (Instant Market Value).

acceptance_criteria.statement: Given a motors marketplace planning a dealer price tool and online reservations, the reader uses the dated automotive record to say what each requires.
acceptance_criteria.probe: A motors marketplace that rates every car's price in five bands plans a dealer tool showing how a price cut would move the band and the car's search position, and wants to switch on online reservations for all dealers' stock. Using only this chapter: what does the public record show, and what should the marketplace put in place for each?
acceptance_criteria.expected: mobile.de, CarGurus and Autotrader publish five-band price ratings, and mobile.de shows dealers how a price change moves search position; once a rating feeds ranking and dealer tools the model shapes the prices it learns from, so it needs an owner, evaluation on band accuracy and boundary clustering, a no-rating path and ranking-change review. Autotrader's Deal Builder reached 137,000 full reservations in a year while forecourts fell in the second half and dealers cut paid stock, and its auto-rollout was paused for 'request a reservation'; reservations must be opt-in, configurable per dealer and reversible. Owning cars is a different business, from which CarGurus' CarOffer and OLX Autos retreated.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reader of the opening alone (the callouts and the paragraphs before the first heading) can predict the chapter's questions, its evidence and where it ends.
acceptance_criteria.probe: After reading only the callouts and the paragraphs before the first heading: what questions will this chapter ask, what kind of evidence will it use, and how will it end?
acceptance_criteria.expected: Three questions asked of each company (what the public contract reveals, what the reported numbers say about the systems behind them, where the marketplace's responsibility ends); evidence from integration API manuals, investor reports and engineering posts for mobile.de, Autotrader UK, AutoScout24 and CarGurus, with OLX Autos as the brief contrast; tests of feed contracts, change feeds and model governance; a comparison with Veldmark's Motorvane and the close of Part IX's cases.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reverse outline of the chapter, written without the spec, lists the same controlling ideas in the same order as the post spec's sections and paragraphs.

Every statement about mobile.de, Autotrader, AutoScout24 or CarGurus's internal systems that no cited source documents sits in a callout or figure caption labeled as inference, and every company fact outside those labels carries its source and publication year.
acceptance_criteria.probe: Is there any sentence outside an `INFERENCE, NOT DOCUMENTED` callout or a labeled figure caption that describes how mobile.de, Autotrader, AutoScout24 or CarGurus builds or runs a system without a dated source, or a company fact with no source and year?
acceptance_criteria.expected: None. Undocumented internals appear only in labeled inference callouts or captions; each company fact names its source and year in the sentence or the timeline; the author's interpretation is marked 'my reading' or sits in the Chief Architect's view.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The chapter's final section performs Part IX's closing: it says what the six cases show together that no single case shows, why it matters, and returns to the part introduction's test of which patterns the record supports, which it only fails to contradict, and where it is silent, before handing off to the toolkit.

thesis.question: What do the automotive leaders' published dealer contracts, investor reports and engineering posts reveal about a dealer-fed listing system, and where does the marketplace's responsibility end?
thesis.claim: Because a car has a machine-readable identity, arrives through dealer software and is supplied by the customer who pays, the automotive leaders' public record is their architecture: mobile.de's and Autotrader's published dealer contracts (accountable integrators, idempotent creates, serialized writes, a change feed with replay) are the documented answer to unmanaged feeds; their five-band price ratings, once shown to dealers alongside search position or used in ranking, shape the prices they learn from and need ranking-model governance; and the marketplace's responsibility ends where platform-controlled state on a dealer's stock stops being opt-in and reversible, as Deal Builder's friction and the CarOffer and OLX Autos retreats show.
thesis.disputed_by: The view that a dealer feed is an import job each marketplace tunes privately, that a price rating is a neutral label rather than a model with consequences, and that a marketplace should move into reservations, guarantees and owning cars to capture more of each sale.
thesis.so_what: A Chief Architect publishes the professional supply contract before building the importer and treats vendor certification as a release gate; publishes change with a stated delay and replay window, 24 hours by default; registers any price rating that labels or orders results as a ranking model with an owner, band-boundary monitoring and a no-rating path; derives billing counts from the same inventory state search shows; makes every platform-set transactional state opt-in, configurable per dealer and reversible; and runs data APIs as a business line with their own service levels.
thesis.how_why: Nine-tenths of automotive supply arrives through dealer feeds. mobile.de's Seller API and Ad Stream document transfer service providers as integration principals, idempotent creates, one write at a time per ad, a taxonomy keyed to a vehicle derivative and a change feed with a 24-hour catch-up window, and its price planner links price to search position. mobile.de, CarGurus and Autotrader all publish five-band price ratings or flags. Autotrader UK discloses its levers, serves about 155 million data-API calls a month, and by March 2026 had more than 6,700 retailers on Deal Builder with 137,000 full reservations in the year, while forecourts fell in the second half and dealers cut paid stock. CarGurus' 2025 annual report records the wind-down of CarOffer, and Prosus exited OLX Autos from 2023. mobile.de's internals, AutoScout24's product platform and every valuation method remain unpublished.

supporting_claims.claim: A car's machine-readable identity, supply written by dealer software and a supplier who is also the paying customer make the automotive leaders' public contracts and investor disclosures a description of their listing systems.

mobile.de's and Autotrader's published dealer contracts (accountable integrators, idempotent creates, serialized writes, stable error keys, a change feed with replay, a notice period for breaking changes) are the documented answer to unmanaged dealer feeds.

Five-band price ratings, once they feed ordering or dealer tools that show a price change moving the band or the search position, become a control loop that shapes the prices the model learns from, and need the governance of a ranking model.

When the supplier pays, inventory state is billing state and a platform-controlled state on a dealer's stock is a commercial-model change; the marketplace's responsibility ends where such states stop being opt-in and reversible, as Deal Builder's friction and the CarOffer and OLX Autos retreats show.

The evidence is uneven and stops at internals (mobile.de's services, AutoScout24's product platform, every valuation method), so each fact is dated, each inference labeled, and the book's patterns and Veldmark's Motorvane are tested only as far as the record reaches.

role.contribution: Tests the supply contract, change feed and model-governance patterns in the vertical that publishes its contracts, marks where the marketplace's responsibility ends, and closes Part IX with the hand-off to the toolkit.

additional_patterns.applies_to: mobile-de to olx-autos: the two European listing platforms first (mobile.de's contracts, then AutoScout24's platform), then Autotrader UK, CarGurus and OLX Autos in order of how far each reaches up the transaction ladder (reservations, wholesale, owning cars)
across-cases to evidence-stops: cross-case views (price products side by side, options, risks, other verticals, gaps)
chief-architect to questions: rules from the record, their test against the book and Veldmark, and questions for the reader's group

flow.rationale: Reading rules, the timeline and the vertical's properties come first because every later sentence is a dated fact, a reading or an inference, and the properties explain why the companies publish what they publish. The companies are grouped one per section because each documents a different layer (API contracts, investor levers, platform posts, a 10-K) and the record cannot be phased (decision of 2026-10-19); mobile.de leads because its contracts set the write path, change feed and price rating that every later section refers back to; AutoScout24 follows as the other European listing platform, whose record is platform only, so that Autotrader, CarGurus and OLX Autos then run up the transaction ladder without a break (decision of 2026-11-12, after both round-1 flow readers found AutoScout24 out of place between Autotrader and CarGurus); OLX Autos closes the group as the contrast that bounds the ladder. The cross-case views come only after all companies because each uses facts from several of them; the evidence limits close that group so the rules that follow do not outrun them. The author's rules, the comparison and the questions apply what the record has shown, and the conclusion closes the case and Part IX together because this is Part IX's last case.

hook.content: This last case of Part IX tests the book's patterns in the vertical whose marketplaces are the clearest about their architecture, because they have to be.

sections.heading: Why Automotive Behaves Differently
sections.controlling_idea: Four properties of the automotive profile (strong item identity, software-mediated professional supply, a supplier who pays, a high-ticket item of uncertain value) shape the architecture the case reads, and price evaluation is the vertical's signature data product.

advances_thesis.how: Explains why the record is architectural and introduces the price-rating thread.

transition_in.carries_over: The dated events and the transaction ladder.
transition_in.introduces: The properties of the vertical every case is read against.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Four properties of the automotive profile, developed in vertical-requirements, matter for reading this case.

evidence.what: Strong item identity (VIN, UK plate, HSN/TSN; attributes decoded, not typed), professional software-mediated supply (DMS uploads; the write path is an API for vendors), the supplier pays (inventory state is billing state), high ticket and uncertain value (price guidance, history and finance as data products), each with where the case shows it.
evidence.shows: Shows what each property means for the architecture and which company's record shows it.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Price evaluation, rating an asking price against a model of market value, is the vertical's signature data product and gets its own cross-case section.

sections.heading: mobile.de: An Architecture Written in Its APIs
sections.controlling_idea: mobile.de publishes no engineering blog, but its Seller API, Search API and Ad Stream manuals and its 2026 releases document an accountable dealer write path, a price rating as a contract, a change feed with a 24-hour replay window, and a price tool that links price to search position.

advances_thesis.how: Gives the fullest documented dealer contract, change feed and price rating, and the record's clearest sign that price feeds ranking.

flow.rationale: From the business and its market (ownership, non-exclusive inventory) to why the documents are the evidence, then the write path, the price rating, the read path and change feed, and finally ranking and the 2026 product layer, where the price-rating thread meets ranking.

transition_in.carries_over: The four properties and the price-rating thread.
transition_in.introduces: The company whose API manuals show them most completely.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: mobile.de's history, segment revenue and scale are public, but its ownership as of October 2026 is not fully clear.

evidence.what: Founded 1996, bought by eBay 2004, part of Adevinta from 25 June 2021; 2023 segment revenue €432 million (€408 million classifieds, €24 million advertising); more than 1.6 million listed vehicles and 140 million visits a month as 2025 averages; reported IPO-or-sale process (October 2025); 'Adevinta subsidiary' (August 2026); Bundeskartellamt names Oak Germany Buyer GmbH as parent (8 October 2026).
evidence.source: Adevinta Annual Report 2023 (2024); mobile.de newsroom (2026); PYMNTS relaying the FT (2025); Bundeskartellamt (2026)
evidence.shows: Shows a large, almost purely classifieds business whose current owner the public record does not settle.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: In a dealer-fed vertical inventory is not exclusive, so a marketplace differentiates through audience, data products and workflow rather than supply lock-in.

evidence.what: The Bundeskartellamt's clearance: mobile.de's 'starke Marktposition', AutoScout24 a 'starker Wettbewerber', consumers and dealers 'häufig mehrere Plattformen parallel', platforms offering 'Datenexport zu anderen Plattformen'.
evidence.source: Bundeskartellamt, 2026
evidence.shows: Shows in the regulator's words that the same car is on several marketplaces.

transition_in.introduces: What it records about the market.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: No mobile.de engineering blog was found, so the architectural evidence is its integration documentation, which is unusually complete.

transition_in.carries_over: Differentiation through data products and workflow.
transition_in.introduces: Where the evidence for those systems has to come from.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The Seller API manual defines who may write and how: integrators are accountable principals, creates are idempotent and writes to one ad serialized, freshness is a separate field, vehicle identity is carried as codes, bulk XML upload exists beside the REST API, and the resource list is a product map.

evidence.what: 'Seller API Access can be granted to Transfer Service Providers and Self-Uploading Dealers registered with mobile.de'; the X-Mobile-Insertion-Request-Id header and HTTP 303 on retry; 'Do not send multiple requests for the same ad at the same time'; renewalDate; hsn, tsn and schwackeCode; seller-inventory-key and customerNumber in the XML upload.
evidence.source: mobile.de Seller API manual, Seller-API reference and XML upload manual, n.d. (read October 2026)
evidence.shows: Shows each contract term in the manual's own words.

transition_in.introduces: Its write path.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Taken together, mobile.de treats the integration vendor as an accountable party, makes retries safe and puts ordering responsibility on the client in writing, and each choice removes a class of Feed Roulette incident.

transition_in.introduces: What they add up to against Feed Roulette.

advances_thesis.how: Names the published contract as the answer to unmanaged feeds.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The price rating is part of the same contract: five labels, a preview endpoint returning each band's euro range before an ad exists, a reason when no rating is available, and recalculation when images arrive.

evidence.what: VERY_GOOD_PRICE to HIGH_PRICE; a vehicle 'that has not been created yet'; 'a reason will be provided'; 'If images are uploaded later (at any time), the price rating will be recalculated including the image data.'
evidence.source: mobile.de Seller API manual, n.d. (read October 2026)
evidence.shows: Shows the rating specified as an API resource with explicit states.

transition_in.introduces: The price rating inside it.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Three design choices are visible in the rating: a band with published boundaries rather than a point estimate, an explicit no-rating state with a reason, and recomputation when any input changes.

evidence.what: Figure 2: a price rating designed as a contract (band, no-rating slot, recalculation on new photos).
evidence.shows: Shows the three choices in one picture.

transition_in.introduces: The design choices it reveals.

advances_thesis.how: Sets out the rating's documented design before the loop is discussed.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The Search API lets dealers embed their mobile.de listings on their own sites and carries the consumption, emissions and CO2-cost data German labeling rules require.

transition_in.carries_over: The write path and the rating.
transition_in.introduces: The interfaces that let others read the inventory.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Ad Stream is a WebSocket change feed with two event types, a contract-dependent delay, one connection per user and a catch-up mode that replays 24 hours of missed events.

evidence.what: AD_CREATE_OR_UPDATE and AD_DELETE; 'one connection per user'; catchup=true; 'the historical events are kept for 24 hours'; a test endpoint with 'only 10% of all events' and 60 seconds of extra delay.
evidence.source: mobile.de Ad Stream manual, n.d. (read October 2026)
evidence.shows: Shows a published change-feed contract with a stated retention.

transition_in.carries_over: The Search API as one read interface.
transition_in.introduces: The second, a change feed.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The 24-hour replay window is a public benchmark for how long a consumer may be disconnected before it needs a full resynchronization, and the external contracts imply an internal design that is shown only as a labeled inference.

evidence.what: INFERENCE, NOT DOCUMENTED: a log of listing state changes feeding Ad Stream, a price-rating service called synchronously and asynchronously, per-ad serialization of writes.
evidence.shows: Shows the implied design kept apart from documented fact.

evidence.what: Figure 3: a plausible reference flow consistent with the public API documentation, not a description of mobile.de's systems.
evidence.shows: Shows safe retries, rescoring on photos and a delayed change feed with a 24-hour replay window.

transition_in.introduces: What that number tells consumers and what the contracts imply inside.

advances_thesis.how: Turns the feed into a benchmark and labels the inference.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: mobile.de's ranking is documented only by a 2024 conference abstract (learning to rank with XGBoost under a 30 ms latency target), which does not name the model's features.

evidence.what: 'millions of searches daily' and a 'strict latency SLA <30ms'.
evidence.source: Berlin Buzzwords, June 2024
evidence.shows: Shows how little of ranking is public.

transition_in.introduces: The thinly documented ranking.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The July 2026 platform update says more about the dealer-side product layer: AI lead tools now handle dealers' leads, two releases add data to the listing, and a Preis-Planer simulates how price steps affect days on market, the price rating and search position.

evidence.what: AI reply suggestions produce 45% of written replies; Lead API into CRM systems; 91% of answered calls outside opening hours; Preis-Planer in 2% steps; Stellantis leasing offers (June) and CARFAX checks (September).
evidence.source: mobile.de newsroom, 2026
evidence.shows: Shows the dealer workflow products and the one that ties price to search position.

transition_in.introduces: A 2026 release that says more.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: My reading is that the Preis-Planer is the most revealing sentence in the public record: it confirms that price relative to the market model affects ranking at mobile.de, which makes the price-rating model part of the ranking function.

transition_in.introduces: Why it matters more than the other products.

advances_thesis.how: Shows the loop visible in public.

sections.heading: AutoScout24: The Platform Story
sections.controlling_idea: AutoScout24's public record is almost entirely about its engineering platform, the best-dated platform history of the four, and shows an acquirer's platform absorbing another marketplace at the account and identity layer.

advances_thesis.how: Shows the platform layer documented and the product platform not.

transition_in.carries_over: mobile.de's integration contracts, the other European listing platform's record.
transition_in.introduces: A European rival whose public record is almost all engineering platform.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Unlike mobile.de, AutoScout24 documents its platform rather than its contracts, and its platform history runs from a 2014–2018 re-architecture onto AWS, through a 2025 consolidation of 110 AWS accounts from Trader, to a 2026 platform of nearly 1,000 services.

evidence.what: 'the largest pan-European online car market'; Hellman & Friedman purchase in 2020 (reported €2.84 billion); Project Tatsu from November 2014, 'AWS first' and 'shared nothing' (InfoQ, 2016); bounded-context microservices, 'some' using Kafka (2018); '110 AWS accounts' with 'zero downtime' (August 2025); 994 services, 107 APIs, 2,700 requests per second, 30 TB, more than 270 engineers (careers page, read October 2026); EKS, Argo CD, Backstage and a read-only AI debugging agent (July 2026).
evidence.source: InfoQ 2016; AutoScout24 Tech Blog 2018, 2025, 2026; careers page, n.d.
evidence.shows: Shows a dated platform history in three steps.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The record says little about AutoScout24's listing, ranking or pricing systems, but in my reading it does show an acquirer's platform absorbing another marketplace at the account and identity layer, without any public sign that the product platforms were merged.

transition_in.introduces: What it leaves out and what it still shows.

sections.heading: Autotrader UK: The Economics Disclosed
sections.controlling_idea: Autotrader's results disclose the levers of its revenue, its data business and the cost of Deal Builder, showing that paid-stock counts are revenue, that partner data APIs are a governed B2B product, and that a platform-set state on dealer stock is a commercial-model change.

advances_thesis.how: Gives the documented economics of a dealer-paid marketplace and the friction of platform-set state.

flow.rationale: From the company's disclosed totals to the three revenue levers and the stock lever, then the data APIs and how their contract is run, then Deal Builder, which uses the stock lever to show what platform-set state cost, and last the platform evidence, which is the thinnest and dated (moved after Deal Builder on 2026-11-12, after both round-2 flow readers found it breaking the thread from the stock lever to Deal Builder).

conclusion.heading: What the Cases Show Together
conclusion.synthesis: The automotive record shows the limit as well as the pattern (the leaders went deeper into data and workflow and stepped back from price risk), and read together the six verdict tables of Part IX sort the book's patterns into three groups: supported by dated evidence (share the uniform layers, contracts at the supply boundary, the search index as a rebuildable read model, models governed by the decision they drive, separability under a change of owner), not contradicted (product convergence last and with its own case, since no public convergence completed), and silent (how any group runs search, ranking or listing services across brands after 2024).
conclusion.so_what: A Chief Architect can cite the public record for the layers to share, the separability to design in and the contracts and model governance to publish, and should treat a product-platform convergence as a bet the record has not shown paying off.
